title: Battle of Cannae
summary: Execute the encirclement, then seize all three Roman camps before their reserves can restore the line.
teaching_goal: Nothing new is taught here. The ridge, the bait and the beheading are all things you already know; Cannae only asks whether you can run three of them at once against four times your number.
narrative_intent: Hannibal's masterpiece becomes a prolonged operational battle, not a single frontal collision.
historical_context: 216 BC: beside the Aufidus, Hannibal's deliberately yielding center drew a much larger Roman infantry mass forward while African infantry attacked its flanks and Carthaginian cavalry closed the rear. Two Roman camps supported the army.

victory_conditions.description: Crush all three Roman camps and seal the iron tomb shut. No escape.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Your command falls — and the wings fold inward.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Hold the ruins. Force the Romans to fight on two grounds at once.

stages.title: Take the allied camp
stages.description: Turn the nearest Roman allied camp south of the field.
stages.hint: It is the closest camp to your hill; take it before the wings close.

stages.title: Take the consular town
stages.description: Seize Varro's town at the centre of the Roman line.
stages.hint: The centre gives way once the wings are wrapped around it.

stages.title: Take the river camp
stages.description: Close the encirclement on the Aufidus camp to the north.
stages.hint: With the river camp taken there is nowhere left for the legions to reform.

stages.title: Kill the consular commanders
stages.description: Finish the officers inside the ring.
stages.hint: Their troops leave the field with them.

actions.text: Fix the Roman center in place. Keep both cavalry wings active.
Roman reserves are entering from the northern camp. Close the pocket faster.
Second-wave Roman cavalry is maneuvering for your rear. Rebalance your flanks.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Eighty thousand. I would rather you heard the number than saw it, because seeing it takes most of a morning. Varro has the command today, and Varro believes in going forward. Stand wherever you like.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: So the centre gave and the wings did not. That was well done, and I say so, and I was inside it. Rome has lost an army and a ring for every knight in it. Rome has not yet lost anything that matters.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: You bent us and we did not break, and that is the only sentence anyone will need. Gather your dead off the Aufidus. The river runs slow here; they will be a long time going by.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: You have the allied camp. Socii - allies. They were promised land for this war, and you have just handed them the first piece of it face down.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Varro's town. Varro is not in it; Varro is out front, being brave at other people. Enjoy the walls. I never needed them.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The Aufidus camp. So the ring closes. I told the Senate a ring was what he wanted. They told me I was old.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Here they come - the whole consular line, in step, at Varro's tempo. Eighty thousand men do not turn. Remember that when you want them to.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The allied wing is at your works. Italians, mostly. They fight for Rome because the alternative is fighting Rome, which is a very persuasive argument.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Your men are going down in the centre. I know - that is where you put the Gauls, and Gauls are for spending. It is still a great many funerals.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Hannibal is down. The Senate will strike a coin. I shall keep one and never spend it, which I am told is what he would have done.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The allied wing is down to a handful. I have counted them twice, because there was time. Whatever happens next on this field, remember someone counted.

theme: The battlefield becomes a closing iron tomb.
